messages:
incident-bot: PAGER — HIGH severity: GPU inference pool autoscaling degraded. Queue growth observed on `video-gpu` pool (gpu_queue_length > 120 for 6m). Some requests experiencing >60s queue wait. Incident ID INC-3945. Paging oncall: @sana. Runbook: https://redwood/runbooks/gpu-autoscale

sana: ack. I'm on it. grabbing metrics and runbook.

maria: fyi I'm nearby — will join for metrics-adapter checks. initial hypothesis: external metrics pipeline (prometheus -> adapter -> HPA) lagging; HPA not seeing up-to-date queue_length.

leo: seeing high scrape latency on prometheus: `prometheus_target_latency_seconds_bucket{job=\"gpu-exporter\"}` is spiking. Also metrics-adapter logs show repeated timeouts: `GET /apis/custom.metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1/... timed out`.

james: copying logs.
```bash
kubectl -n infra logs deployment/metrics-adapter -c adapter --tail=200
# sample tail showing timeout errors and backlog
# 2026-03-15T12:01:02Z ERROR adapter.go:429 request timeout after 30s
# 2026-03-15T12:02:04Z WARN adapter.go:312 queue depth=194
```

sana: thanks. trying soft mitigation: patching HPA to fallback to cpu metric temporarily so autoscaler can scale while adapter recovers.

leo: recommended command to patch HPA to a safe CPU target (manual fallback):
```bash
kubectl -n workloads patch hpa/gpu-pool-hpa --type='json' -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/metrics","value":[{"type":"Resource","resource":{"name":"cpu","target":{"type":"Utilization","averageUtilization":45}}}] }]'
```

sana: executed patch, scaling should be allowed now. also manually bumped Deployment replicas for `gpu-worker` from 6 -> 10 to provide immediate capacity.

amanda-cs: on customer impact — CS notes: two enterprise tenants (org-acme, org-nomad) reported inference failures (503) and high tail latency starting ~12:00 UTC. tickets created. will message customers with ETA when we have recovery.

maria: restarting metrics-adapter to clear backlog.
```bash
kubectl -n infra rollout restart deployment/metrics-adapter
# watching pods come back up
```

deploy-bot: deployment/metrics-adapter rollout started (revision: 42 -> 43).

ops-bot: NOTE: autoscaler fallback detected. HPA now evaluating CPU metric. previous external metric not available.

leo: prometheus still showing many pending samples, we should reduce scrape retention and increase replica capacity temporarily — but restarting adapter first is correct.

sana: adapter pods are green again and logs show successful list calls. verifying HPA behavior...

maria: HPA now sees CPU metrics and scaled to 10 replicas; queue length metrics still delayed but queue is draining: `gpu_queue_length` down from 240 -> 30 over 3m.

james: confirming on infra: GPU utilization ~68% across new replicas, queue processing rate back to normal.

amanda-cs: updating customers: "We are seeing an ongoing recovery; throughput restored, some requests that were queued may have timed out. We estimate ~12-15m customer impact window; no data loss. Support ticket IDs: #3421, #3422."

sana: root cause short summary: Prometheus -> metrics-adapter pipeline experienced high scrape latency/timeout (prom scrape backlog + adapter timeouts) which prevented external metric updates -> HPA didn't trigger autoscale -> queue growth -> GPU pool exhausted/requests throttled.

maria: mitigation summary: restarted metrics-adapter, patched HPA to CPU fallback, manually increased replicas as immediate capacity, added short-term extra pool in cloud console for spike capacity.

leo: current action items (short):
- add heartbeat alert for metrics-adapter (if adapter hasn't returned a heartbeat metric in 60s)
- add an HPA fallback policy in platform (auto-fallback to resource metric after 30s of missing external metrics)
- investigate prometheus scrape latency root cause (too many targets / scrape timeout)

james: I'm assigning postmortem to @maria and @sana. will create INC-3945 doc and timeline.

amanda-cs: CS to follow up with customers with RCA once postmortem is ready.

sana: handoff: @james you're on for next 4 hours, I'll go offline in 10m. please monitor queue and adapter heartbeat. link to incident doc: https://redwood/incidents/INC-3945-doc

james: ack taking over. will keep Slack channel updated every 20m.

ops-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: queue length stable <40, autoscaler active using CPU fallback, adapter heartbeat healthy. severity -> MEDIUM.

maria: quick note for followups: consider improving adapter scaling (horizontal autoscaling of adapter) and rate limiting/ingestion window on Prometheus to prevent backlog. also add an internal runbook step to auto-apply HPA fallback for known external metric outages.

amanda-cs: adding those action items to the customer-facing timeline.

incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED (monitoring mode): incident marked resolved; automatic postmortem creation scheduled. If you observed regressions reopen thread.
